title: Installing a Radiant Floor Heat System in a Garage (This Old House)

locations.name: Garage
locations.basis: Explicitly referenced as the space being heated and the pour location in transcript

summary: This This Old House segment documents choosing and installing a radiant floor heating system in a concrete garage slab. After evaluating heating options (gas boiler, electric baseboards, or radiant heat), the team selects a radiant system embedded in the slab to minimize heat loss and heat the space efficiently. The installation uses a pre-fabricated 2x4-foot panel that combines insulation, vapor barrier, and tubing-holding channels. PEX tubing is laid on a 12-inch-on-center grid, starting near the manifold and staggering seams. Tubing entry into the slab is protected by bends, and the slab is reinforced with wire mesh before a four-inch concrete pour. The crew, including local vocational students, completes the pour and finishes the slab, resulting in a heated garage floor.
topics: Tubing grid and 12 inch on-center spacing

sections.title: Option evaluation and radiant-floor choice
sections.description: The presenters discuss multiple heating options for the garage (an in-corner blower, a boiler with hot water, gas, electric baseboard, etc.) and explain why radiant floor heat in a concrete slab is a good candidate: it heats the space efficiently and keeps heat inside the building, with attention to insulation and underfoot warmth.

sections.title: Panel-based installation of radiant tubing
concepts: Starting in the corner near the manifold
Seam staggering to avoid lined seams
sections.description: A pre-fabricated 2x4-foot panel that combines insulation, vapor barrier, and tubing-holding channels is used. PEX tubing is laid on a grid with 12-inch on-center spacing, starting in the corner near the manifold, with seams staggered so they do not align. The system is designed for easy assembly and reliable tube placement.

sections.title: Pour and finish of the concrete slab
concepts: Tubing protection at entry into slab
sections.description: The team notes the routing of tubing into the slab with protective bends, connects to the manifold, and proceeds to pour the concrete to create the heated slab. A wire mesh layer is added for slab strength, and the crew finishes the surface.

sections.title: Wrap-up and context
sections.description: Closing remarks point viewers to other This Old House videos and encourage subscribing for more home improvement content.
